q: Vegetative propagation by cutting and grafting produces offspring that are:
why: No gametes/fertilization involved, so offspring is a clone of parent.

q: Pollen transfer from one flower to another flower on the SAME plant is called:
why: Geitonogamy is pollination between two flowers of the same plant.

q: Which type of pollination occurs between flowers of two genetically different plants?
why: Xenogamy is true cross-pollination between different plants.
Maize is anemophilous, pollen carried by wind to another plant's stigma.

q: A mature anther typically has how many microsporangia (pollen sacs)?
why: Each of the two lobes has two microsporangia, giving 4 in total.

q: The innermost, nourishing wall layer of the microsporangium is the:
why: Tapetum is the innermost layer that nourishes developing pollen grains.

q: In the embryo sac, the egg cell along with two synergids forms the:
why: Egg cell + 2 synergids near the micropylar end form the egg apparatus.

q: In double fertilization, fusion of a male gamete with the two polar nuclei is called:
why: Triple fusion forms the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).

q: A seed that develops without fertilization, as in an apomictic Citrus embryo, is genetically:
why: Apomictic embryos arise from diploid ovule cells without meiosis/fertilization, so they clone the mother plant.

q: A seedless banana fruit forms without fertilization through a process called:
why: Parthenocarpy is fruit development from the ovary without fertilization, giving seedless fruit.
